answer.rationale: Under competitive pricing pressure with doubled churn conversations, promotional_pricing is rejected because memory_73 explicitly warns it materially reduces 30-day retention despite acquisition lift—directly contradicting our primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive are valuable but address different segments and do not directly counter SMB churn acceleration. Simplified onboarding (memory_86, memory_31) has strong retention lift (+3%) but works best as a gradual adoption lever. Activation_messaging (memory_91) produced +11% week-one engagement, +6% activation, and +1% retention lift. The dual effect—improving time-to-value perception while strengthening early commitment—creates friction against churn at the moment accounts are most at-risk. This addresses the immediate crisis by deepening product value realization rather than racing to the bottom on price. A standard_experiment scope allows rapid deployment to at-risk SMB cohorts while preserving ability to layer onboarding improvements and referral mechanics as secondary responses. The approach prioritizes retention quality over acquisition velocity, aligning with long-term revenue sustainability.
